newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HAL WINS BATTLE TO BUY DUTCH FINANCE DAILY.
newsitem.headline: HAL WINS BATTLE TO BUY DUTCH FINANCE DAILY.

text.p: Investment company HAL has signed an 84 million guilder deal to take over Dutch business daily Het Financieele Dagblad together with Willem Sijthoff, a grand nephew of the paper's current owner, the paper said.
Executive director Ria Kuip was not immediately available for comment.
"It is expected that the final transfer of the (non-voting) share certificates will occur on May 21," Financieele Dagblad said, adding the intervening period was for due diligence.
The voting rights remain vested within a foundation controlled by Financieele Dagblad staff.
"The intention is...to keep (economic) ownership and executive control separate (from one another)," the paper said.

The deal ends nearly a decade of wrangling over the sale of the title, with staff at the paper opposing takeovers by potential buyers such as mass circulation daily De Telegraaf and Pearson, publisher of Britain's Financial Times.
These bids had been based on a simultaneous takeover of the staff voting rights.
Under the deal, the staff will gain the option to acquire a 30 percent stake in the paper and appoint two members of the six-strong supervisory board.
HAL and Sijthoff have undertaken to retain a majority holding for at least ten years and not to sell any shares to a publisher during that time.
Staff at the paper have yet to be consulted on the deal, but have backed it in the past as the best guarantee of the title's continued independence.
Management argues that independence from other media groups would enable the paper to choose the most suitable partner for future projects unhampered by possible conflicts of interest.

The paper, which reported a five percent increase in circulation to 41,000 last year, has a distribution agreement with the International Herald Tribune for its English-language weekly and is in the process of setting up a business news service with national news agency ANP.
